sources.title: Marine Personnel Regulations, SOR/2007-115
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2023-12-20 (Justice Canada laws-lois-xml repository); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Full text read from the official Justice Canada XML (github.com/justicecanada/laws-lois-xml, eng/regulations/SOR-2007-115.xml); the laws-lois.justice.gc.ca HTML was not used. Supports: s. 100(uu) (Bridge Watch Rating is a certificate of competency); s. 103 (MED course must be within 5 years of issue, or equivalency; first aid course validity); s. 110(1) (18 years of age on receiving the certificate; sea service started at 16 or older); s. 110(2)-(3) (application at least two weeks before first exam; application valid 1 year); s. 111(b) (medical certificate required before issue; Bridge Watch Rating is not in the exempt list); s. 112 (exams follow TP 2293 procedures); s. 113(1)(a) (pass in a Bridge Watch Rating exam valid 5 years, for life once certificate obtained); s. 170 (Able Seafarer: 36 months deck rating service plus written and practical exams); s. 171 table (Bridge Watch Rating: 6 months bridge watchkeeping sea service, or 2 months after an approved training program; MED basic safety; MED survival craft and rescue boats other than fast rescue boats; steering testimonial per Schedule 3; marine basic first aid; written examination on general seamanship); Schedule 3 to Part 1 (steering testimonial contents and master's declaration, hours at the wheel left blank, no minimum hours stated); s. 213 (deck watch per STCW Code A-VIII/2 Parts 2, 3 and 3-1); s. 216 (deck watch composition: additional person must hold Able Seafarer or Bridge Watch Rating on vessels of 500 GT or more; second additional person on vessels over 1000 GT not anchored or moored); ss. 238 and 247 (equivalent deck watch rules for self-propelled MOUs and foreign vessels); s. 270(3) (colour vision standards apply to Bridge Watch Rating, which is not exempted); ss. 319-323 (hours of rest: 6 consecutive hours in 24 and 16 in 48 for domestic voyages; 10 in 24 and 77 in 7 days, max two periods one at least 6 h, interval max 14 h for unlimited or foreign waters; fatigue to be considered; records). Reproduction of Federal Law Order statement not seen in this research, so marked unclear.

sources.title: Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, SOR/2020-216
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2023-12-20 (Justice Canada XML); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML. Supports: s. 106 (standard and steering magnetic compasses; gyro-compass on near coastal Class 1, unlimited or international voyages; compasses compensated, deviation table or curve kept near the compass); s. 108 (two-way voice communication to emergency steering position); s. 133 (heading or track control system: immediate changeover to manual steering in high traffic density, restricted visibility or other hazardous situations; qualified helmsman available; changeover made by or under supervision of the person in charge of the deck watch; manual steering tested before areas needing special caution and at least once a day); s. 134 (two steering power units in operation in areas needing special caution); s. 135 (changeover instructions and block diagram displayed on bridge and in steering gear compartment); s. 136 (steering gear checked and tested within 12 hours before departure, list of checks; weekly for regular voyages under one week; emergency steering drills at least every three months; record in log); s. 137 (working language for navigational safety); s. 111 (gyro-compass, heading repeater at the emergency steering position and bearing repeater on vessels subject to SOLAS Chapter V); s. 118 (AIS Class A connected to gyro or heading device); s. 140 (field of vision from main steering position at least 60 degrees each side of ahead); s. 209 (float-free EPIRB requirements; manual EPIRB, PLB or DSC handheld worn by the person in charge of the navigational watch); s. 223 (VHF channel 16 watch); ss. 228-229 (EPIRB registration with the Canadian Beacon Registry, update within 30 days; Cospas-Sarsat 406 MHz type approval).

sources.title: Maritime Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, SOR/2010-120
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2026-02-04, last amended 2025-03-26 (Justice Canada XML); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML. Made under Part II of the Canada Labour Code (the 'Canadian Labour Code' named in TP 10936). Supports: s. 2 definition of confined space; s. 14 (stage supports, ropes or tackle safety factor not less than six); s. 144 (fall-protection system for unguarded work areas more than 2.4 m above the nearest permanent safe level, above an open hold or moving machinery, structures over 3 m, one-handed ladder work over 2.4 m; anchor 17.8 kN); s. 147 (drowning hazard: life jacket, safety net or fall protection; emergency equipment and qualified person ready); ss. 165-173 (work permits; no entry into a confined space without a work permit; marine chemist or qualified person assessment; oxygen 19.5 to 23 per cent by volume); s. 229 (code of signals for materials handling equipment, signaller duties); s. 240 (no load over safe working load; SWL marked on equipment). Use for the occupational health and safety lessons.

sources.title: Safe Working Practices Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1467
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2007-07-01 (Justice Canada XML); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML. Named in TP 10936 Edition 2 (OHS competence) and in the BCIT outcomes. Headings: lifting appliances, holds and tanks, fire prevention, hot work, scaffolding and stages, ladders and gangways, electrical, PPE, pressure vessels. Supports s. 52 (stage supports and ropes factor of safety not less than six) and the SWL notice on lifting appliances. Older than the MOHS Regulations; where they overlap, a reviewer should confirm which applies to which vessels.

sources.title: Tackle Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1494
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2007-07-01 (Justice Canada XML); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML. Named in the BCIT Bridge Watch Rating outcomes. Supports the rule that cargo gear must not be loaded beyond its safe working load. Only the headings and SWL rule were checked; deeper use needs a reviewer.

sources.title: Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations, SOR/2012-69
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-12-29, last amended 2021-06-23 (Justice Canada XML); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML. Named in the BCIT outcomes. Supports: s. 30 (oily mixture discharge only through equipment giving an undiluted effluent of not more than 15 ppm, with further conditions); ss. 32-35 (oil transfer operations: continuous two-way voice communication able to order immediate shutdown; lighting 54 lx at connection points and 11 lx in work areas at night; transfer conduits bursting pressure four times design, annual hydrostatic test; slow down or stop if a conduit leaks); Oil Record Book requirements; ss. 100-104 (garbage discharge outside Canadian jurisdiction: floating dunnage 25 nm, other garbage 12 nm, ground garbage 3 nm, no plastics; placards on vessels 12 m or more; garbage management plan for 400 GT or more or 15 persons or more). Garbage and sewage rules inside Canadian waters were not fully read; a reviewer must confirm before any lesson states them.

sources.title: Small Vessel Regulations, SOR/2010-91
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2026-01-19, last amended 2025-12-31 (Justice Canada XML); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML. Supports s. 20 (pyrotechnic distress signals expire four years after date of manufacture; Type A, B, C and D flares may replace rocket parachute flares, multi-star flares, hand flares and smoke signals respectively if approved before the Regulations came into force). Applies to small vessels; larger vessels follow other equipment rules, so lessons must say which vessels a number applies to.

sources.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations, SOR/2001-286
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws (Department of Justice consolidated text)
sources.notes: Read from the official Justice Canada XML, only to confirm the names of the nine UN hazard classes (Class 1 Explosives; 2 Gases; 3 Flammable Liquids; 4 Flammable Solids, spontaneous combustion, water-reactive; 5 Oxidizing Substances and Organic Peroxides; 6 Toxic and Infectious Substances; 7 Radioactive Materials; 8 Corrosives; 9 Miscellaneous). The IMDG Code (IMO, copyrighted, paid) uses the same UN class numbers; it was not read. Use for the dangerous goods awareness lesson, labelled as general awareness only.

sources.title: TP 10936 Bridge Watch Rating Training Course, Edition 2 (HTML version)
sources.publisher: Transport Canada, Marine Safety and Security
sources.notes: The course standard and the main syllabus source. Seen only through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool asked for verbatim quotes (four passes on 2026-10-06); the raw page was not opened. Supports: course incorporates STCW Rating Forming Part of a Navigational Watch plus components of Able Seafarer Deck; 300 hours; ten competences with hours (navigation at support level, steering and helm orders 30; lookout by sight and hearing 40; safe watch 20; emergency equipment 5; survival craft 5; berthing, anchoring, mooring 25; cargo and stores 35; deck equipment and machinery 65; OHS and pollution prevention 40; maintenance and repair 35); full knowledge lists (helm orders in English, magnetic and gyro compass, bridge equipment, high-latitude compass limits, pre-departure steering checks, follow-up and non-follow-up, emergency steering, squat and interaction, ranges, autopilot changeover; lookout reporting in degrees or points, lights, shapes, sound signals, IALA aids, distress signals by sight, sound, radiotelephone and aircraft, radar echoes, steady bearing, watch handover at sea, at anchor and in port; knots, splices, wire, flags A B G H O P Q T Z, draft marks, sounding; safe working practices; pollution; maintenance); entry age 16, certificate age 18; class sizes; written exam approved by TC with 50 multiple-choice questions and 60 per cent pass mark; practical exam by the training provider with 70 per cent pass mark. No copyright or reproduction statement was found by the tool. Paraphrase only.

sources.title: TP 10936E Bridge Watch Rating Training Course, Edition 2, September 2024 (PDF)
sources.publisher: Transport Canada, Marine Safety and Security
sources.edition: Edition 2, September 2024 (2025-03 upload; a 2024-10 upload also exists); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Not read: tc.canada.ca blocked direct download and robots.txt blocked the fetch tool. Listed so a reviewer can check the PDF against the HTML version (bw-tp10936-ed2-html), especially the exam numbers, the equipment checklist and any copyright statement.

sources.title: TP 2293 The Examination and Certification of Seafarers (5th revision)
sources.publisher: Transport Canada, Marine Safety
sources.notes: The examination procedure document named in MPR s. 112. Only the first part of a third-party copy (dieselduck.ca) was summarised by a fetch tool: general pass mark 70 per cent for most TC written exams, 60 per cent for some, and retake waiting periods. The Bridge Watch Rating chapter (reported as Chapter 46) could not be read. A newer edition may exist on tc.canada.ca (https://tc.canada.ca/en/marine-transportation/publications/tp-2293-examination-certification-seafarers), not read. Use only to flag that the TC exam pass mark is unverified.

sources.title: Deck watch requirements for all Canadian and foreign vessels including tug boats operating in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, Ship Safety Bulletin 07/2017
sources.publisher: Transport Canada, Marine Safety and Security
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Supports: deck watch composition under MPR ss. 213 and 216 (additional person on vessels of 5 GT or more; Bridge Watch Rating or Able Seafarer on 500 GT or more; second additional person over 1000 GT); the officer may be the sole look-out only in daylight after careful assessment of weather, visibility, traffic, dangers and with assistance immediately available; issued after tug and barge incidents. Good plain-language source for the watch-system lesson.

sources.title: Mandatory fatigue management training (Revised), Ship Safety Bulletin 01/2026
sources.publisher: Transport Canada, Marine Safety and Security
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Supports: all Canadian seafarers enrolling in MED courses (STCW Basic Safety, Proficiency in Survival Craft and others) must complete the free CCOHS Fatigue Management at Sea e-course; the fatigue certificate must be produced before the MED training certificate is issued; fatigue has been on the TSB Watchlist since 2018. Related page: https://tc.canada.ca/en/marine-transportation/seafarer-certification/managing-fatigue-sea-canada (not read).

sources.title: The Canadian Aids to Navigation System, 2023 Edition
sources.publisher: Canadian Coast Guard, Aids to Navigation Program (Fisheries and Oceans Canada)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool (three passes). The primary source for the buoyage lessons. Supports: combined lateral-cardinal system, IALA Region B; upstream direction defined as from seaward toward the headwaters of a river or into a harbour, starboard hand aids kept to starboard when proceeding upstream; port hand green, flat-topped (can), odd numbers, green cylinder topmark, green Fl 4s or Q 1s light; starboard hand red, conical, even numbers, red cone topmark, red Fl 4s or Q 1s; only lateral buoys numbered; bifurcation buoys with broad band and Fl(2+1) 6s or 10s; cardinal buoys (topmarks, black/yellow, Q/VQ white lights: N continuous, E 3, S 6 plus long flash, W 9); isolated danger (black with red band, two black spheres, Fl(2) 5s or 10s); safe water (red and white vertical stripes, red sphere, Mo(A) 6s or LFl 10s); special buoys (yellow, Fl 4s, ODAS Fl(5) 20s; cautionary, anchorage, mooring, swimming, keep out, control); light rhythm definitions; daybeacons and ranges; radar reflectors, RACONs, retroreflective material. Crown copyright stated; no reproduction permission seen. The tool did not find a Pacific-coast statement on the direction of buoyage.

sources.title: Radio Aids to Marine Navigation 2026, Part 4: General
sources.publisher: Canadian Coast Guard
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool (first 100,000 characters). Supports: MAYDAY, PAN PAN and SECURITE and when each is used; VHF channel 16 (156.8 MHz) and 2182 kHz reserved for distress, urgency, safety and calling; DSC on VHF channel 70 and 2187.5 kHz; bridge-to-bridge channel 13; VTS sector frequencies. Use for the VHF basics lesson; the full ROC-MC syllabus is outside this ticket.

sources.title: Canadian Chart 1: Symbols, Abbreviations and Terms
sources.publisher: Canadian Hydrographic Service
sources.notes: Found in search results only; not opened. The reference for chart symbols in the chart basics lesson (BCIT outcome 8). A writer must read it before citing any symbol.

sources.title: STCW Code Table A-II/4: Specification of minimum standard of competence for ratings forming part of a navigational watch
sources.publisher: International Maritime Organization (text hosted by Massachusetts Maritime Academy, weh.maritime.edu)
sources.edition: STCW Code as amended (2018 page); accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Supports the international competence list the TP 10936 course is built on: steer and comply with helm orders in English (magnetic and gyro compasses, helm orders, autopilot changeover); keep a look-out by sight and hearing (report approximate bearing in degrees or points); contribute to a safe watch (shipboard terms, internal communication and alarm systems, communicate with the OOW, watch relief and handover, information to maintain a safe watch, basic environmental protection); operate emergency equipment (emergency duties and alarm signals, pyrotechnics, EPIRBs and SARTs, avoiding false alerts). IMO text is copyrighted; paraphrase only.

sources.title: IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases, Resolution A.918(22)
sources.publisher: International Maritime Organization (copy hosted by DIRECTEMAR, Chile)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool, which confirmed sections A2/1 Standard Wheel Orders and A2/2 Standard Engine Orders exist but could not extract their text. IMO page: https://imo.org/en/OurWork/Safety/Pages/StandardMarineCommunicationPhrases.aspx. A writer must read A2/1 and A2/2 directly before the helm orders lesson is final. Paraphrase only.

sources.title: Standard wheel orders (copy of the IMO standard marine phrases list)
sources.publisher: Personal website hosted on oocities.org (archive of GeoCities)
sources.notes: Low-authority secondary copy, seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Lists: midships; port/starboard five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five; hard-a-port/starboard; nothing to port/starboard; meet her; steady; ease to five/ten/fifteen/twenty; steady as she goes; keep the buoy/mark/beacon on port/starboard side; report if she does not answer the wheel; finished with wheel; and that all wheel orders are repeated by the helmsman and checked by the OOW. Use only to cross-check bw-imo-smcp-a918; do not cite alone.

sources.title: STCW assessment RFPNW-1K: helm orders (U.S. National Assessment Guidelines, hosted by Massachusetts Maritime Academy)
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Maritime Academy (weh.maritime.edu)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. U.S. practice (uses 'right/left rudder' wording, which differs from the port/starboard wording of the IMO SMCP used in Canada). Useful for the repeat-back and report pattern (repeat the order, report rudder position, report heading every 10 degrees, report 'steady on' the course) and the U.S. performance standard of steering within plus or minus 3 degrees offshore or 2 degrees near coastal. Do not present the U.S. wording or tolerances as Canadian requirements.

sources.title: STW 40/7/55: Chapter VIII of the STCW Convention and Code, review of section A-VIII/2 part 3
sources.publisher: IMO Sub-Committee on Standards of Training and Watchkeeping (copy in the IMarEST library)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Quotes the STCW Code A-VIII/2 Part 3-1 look-out paragraph (look-out maintained at all times per COLREG Rule 5, to keep continuous vigilance by sight and hearing and all available means, fully appraise the situation and risk of collision, stranding and other dangers, and detect ships or aircraft in distress, shipwrecked persons, wrecks and debris) and the handover rule (do not hand over to a relief believed not capable). The sole-look-out and helmsman paragraphs were not extracted. A writer should read the current STCW Code A-VIII/2 directly.

sources.title: MGN 137 (M+F): Look-out during periods of darkness and restricted visibility
sources.publisher: Maritime and Coastguard Agency (United Kingdom)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. UK guidance, not Canadian law: advises against the OOW acting as sole look-out in darkness and calls for additional look-outs in restricted visibility. Supporting context only for the lookout lesson.

sources.title: Pub. 102 International Code of Signals (1969 edition, revised 2020)
sources.publisher: U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (copy hosted by the U.S. Coast Guard National Maritime Center)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool, which reported the header 'No copyright claimed under Title 17 U.S.C.' (U.S. Government work); a reviewer should confirm that statement on the PDF. Supports the single-letter signal meanings used in the flags lesson, including the nine TP 10936 letters: A diver down, keep well clear at slow speed; B taking in, discharging or carrying dangerous goods; G I require a pilot (fishing vessels: hauling nets); H pilot on board; O man overboard; P in harbour, all persons report on board, vessel about to proceed to sea; Q vessel healthy, request free pratique; T keep clear, engaged in pair trawling; Z I require a tug (fishing vessels: shooting nets).

sources.title: The American Practical Navigator (Bowditch), Pub. 9, Volume 2, Chapter 5: Compass Conversions
sources.publisher: U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (copy hosted by thenauticalalmanac.com)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Supports definitions of variation (angle between geographic and magnetic meridians), deviation (magnetic north to compass north, caused by the vessel's own magnetism, changes with heading), compass error (algebraic sum of variation and deviation), the True-Variation-Magnetic-Deviation-Compass order, easterly errors make compass readings lower than true and westerly higher, and gyro error named east or west. U.S. Government work, but no copyright statement was seen on this hosted copy.

sources.title: Seaman (NAVEDTRA 14067), Nonresident Training Course
sources.publisher: U.S. Navy, Naval Education and Training Professional Development and Technology Center (copy hosted by Nashville Sea Cadets)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool (first 100,000 characters). States 'Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.' Supports general lookout practice (relative bearings clockwise from the bow in degrees, 11.25 degrees per point, reporting to the bridge) and the repeat-back principle for steering orders. U.S. Navy wording (right/left rudder, 'sir') is not Canadian merchant practice; use for concepts, not phrasing.

sources.title: Bridge Watch Rating (MSSM 1030) course outline
sources.publisher: British Columbia Institute of Technology
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. A BC approved provider's 19 learning outcomes: fibre and wire rope; knots, bends, hitches; splicing; chains, shackles, slips; anchoring and mooring; helmsman and lookout duties; reading navigational instruments and reporting to the OOW; chart features and basic chartwork; buoyage (international system); Rules of the Road; vessel types and shipboard terms; cargoes, derricks, cranes; ship stability and construction; rigging; maintenance; vessel organisation; personal and vessel documentation; marine emergencies; Safe Working Practices, Tackle, and Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations. Shows provider topics beyond TP 10936 Ed. 2 (chartwork, stability). Copyrighted provider text; use only as a topic checklist.

sources.title: Bridge Watch Rating, Associate Certificate, Full-time (2933ACERT)
sources.publisher: British Columbia Institute of Technology
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Supports: 17 weeks full time; courses ROC-MC, STCW Basic Safety, STCW Proficiency in Survival Craft, Marine Basic First Aid, Bridge Watch Rating (MSSM 1030); entry at 18 with a CDN and a TC marine medical for deck service (reported as valid 2 years); Fatigue Management at Sea before MED courses; 90 per cent attendance and 70 per cent aggregate pass; four months of sea-time remission, two more months of sea time needed for TC certification.

sources.title: Bridge Watch Rating program
sources.publisher: Camosun College
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. BC provider: 17 weeks; skills list (lookout, steering, communication systems, anchoring and mooring, emergencies, environmental protection, cargo, ropes and chains); bundled certificates (TC Bridge Watch Rating training certificate, WHMIS, ROC-MC, SVOP, Marine Basic First Aid, STCW Basic Safety, Proficiency in Survival Craft); CDN and seafarer's medical required. Topic checklist only.

sources.title: Bridge Watch Rating (Marine Training Centre)
sources.publisher: Holland College
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Supports: 11 weeks, 300 hours; entry at 18 with TC marine medical (not colour blind), STCW Basic Safety, Survival Craft and Marine Basic First Aid; 90 per cent attendance and 70 per cent final course mark 'per TP 10936' (conflicts with TP 10936's 60 per cent written exam pass mark); steering testimonial showing 10 hours steering; 60 days of sea service after the course; claims 60 days gives a certificate for Canadian waters and six months gives an unrestricted international certificate (not found in the MPR; flagged).

sources.title: Bridge Watch Program, Technical Certificate (2018 calendar)
sources.publisher: Fisheries and Marine Institute of Memorial University of Newfoundland
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Older calendar: 16 weeks in class, 3 weeks safety training, 60-day sea placement with testimonials and a training record book, after which students 'qualify for the Transport Canada Bridge Watch Rating Certification Exam'. Evidence that a TC exam may follow the course; conflicts or overlaps with TP 10936 Ed. 2's course exam. Flagged.

sources.title: Bridge Watch Rating course (North)
sources.publisher: Arctic Marine (formerly Western Arctic Marine Training Centre, wamtc.ca)
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. 15 weeks; modules: chartwork and navigation, collision regulations, bridge equipment and aids, seamanship and deck operations, bridge watchkeeping, emergency response, marine communications, safety and regulations; graduates need 10 hours at the helm and 60 days of sea time before TC issues the certificate of competency. Topic checklist only.

sources.title: Bridge Watchman (vocational training profile)
sources.publisher: Trades Training BC
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. BC overview of the BCIT program and the job (lookout, steering, communication systems, ropes and chains, anchoring, emergencies, cargo). Context only.

sources.title: Introduction to the Bridge Watch Rating Study Guide
sources.publisher: Maritime Study Guides
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool (the guide index page was blocked). States 6 months of sea time recorded as 'Other: Bridge Watch Duties' and that the exam is administered by Transport Canada. Commercial study guide: never copy its questions or text.

sources.title: Canada Bridge Watch Rating practice exams overview
sources.publisher: Open Exam Prep
sources.notes: Low-authority. Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Repeats TP 10936 (50 questions, 60 per cent written, 70 per cent practical) and gives topic weights that appear to be derived from the TP 10936 teaching hours (for example 13 per cent lookout = 40/300 hours). Do not cite for facts; listed so reviewers know where the 'weights' idea came from.

sources.title: Point System (nautical)
sources.publisher: Wikipedia
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. CC BY-SA. Supports: 32 points at 11.25 degrees; relative positions named from the bow, beam and quarter (dead ahead, fine on the bow, broad on the bow, abeam, broad on the quarter, dead astern); example reports such as 'two points forward of the starboard beam'. Secondary; pair with bw-navedtra-14067-seaman.

sources.title: Draft (hull)
sources.publisher: Wikipedia
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. CC BY-SA. Supports: metric draft marks one decimetre high at two-decimetre intervals, read at the bottom of the figure; imperial marks 6 inches high at 12-inch intervals; marks on both sides near bow and stern and often amidships. Secondary; a reviewer should confirm Canadian practice.

sources.title: Search and rescue transponder
sources.publisher: Wikipedia
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. CC BY-SA. Supports: radar SART responds only to 9 GHz X-band (3 cm) radar; shows a line of 12 dots about 0.64 nm apart, becoming arcs and then circles within about 1 nm; triggered by X-band radar within about 8 nm. Secondary; prefer an IMO or CCG source if found.

sources.title: General emergency signal
sources.publisher: Wikipedia
sources.notes: Seen through a fetch-and-summarise tool. CC BY-SA. Supports: general emergency alarm of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle and alarm system (SOLAS / LSA Code); on hearing it, collect life jacket and go to the muster station; the abandon ship order is given by the master by voice. The Canadian regulatory basis (Vessel Construction and Equipment Regulations, SOR/2023-257, which repealed the Life Saving Equipment Regulations, and TP 14475) was not confirmed.
